# Verification analysis: alias-based-policy-rhel9

Job: `2026-09-05__12-23-47`

This report explains the verifier decisions recorded for this job. It interprets the saved evidence; it does not rerun the task or independently inspect the expired clusters.

## Task

> `node1` routes between `lan-a` and `lan-b`. Permit `node2` to reach `node3`
> on TCP ports 8080, 8443 and 9000, expressing that set of ports as a single
> named object on `node1` and referring to the object from the rule instead of
> writing one rule for each port.

## Trial `alias-based-policy-rhel9__esJTQtb`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** The executor satisfied the task's core contract: a single OPNsense port alias 'node3_svc_ports' (8080/8443/9000) was created under the correct model path and referenced by exactly one firewall pass rule on node1, rather than one rule per port. End-to-end testing confirmed node2 can reach node3 on all three named ports through node1's routing and pf, that an out-of-set port (9999) remains blocked, and that the reverse direction (node3->node2) is blocked by default-deny. A real secondary blocker (node3's local firewalld silently dropping forwarded traffic) was correctly diagnosed and fixed. The provider-wide restart protocol was executed competently on all three nodes with clear pre/post boot-identity evidence and functional re-verification after each restart, corroborated by the fixed lifecycle snapshots. The main shortfall is operational hygiene: several temporary diagnostic files were left behind on node2 and node3 despite the executor's claim of cleanup, and two diagnostic packages were installed on node2 and never removed.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.550 | 0.880 | 109/15 (+7 dropped) |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **R1 — Satisfied:** Create a single named port object (alias) on node1 covering TCP 8080, 8443, and 9000
  - **Why:** config.xml under the correct OPNsense/Firewall/Alias model path defines one alias 'node3_svc_ports' of type 'port' with content 8080/8443/9000 (cmd-8f36cb26600349ff, cmd-3970d1546b4649d0). pf compiles it into the table node3_svc_ports = { 8080 8443 9000 } (cmd-796e7f29c7a14152). An initial attempt using the legacy top-level <aliases> element silently failed pf compilation and was corrected (cmd-bb644861f4fe4ec0 through cmd-8f36cb26600349ff), and the final state was verified working.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-8f36cb26600349ff`, `cmd-3970d1546b4649d0`, `cmd-796e7f29c7a14152`, `cmd-c19dca8eb6914bb8`
- **R2 — Satisfied:** The firewall rule permitting node2->node3 must reference the alias by name rather than one rule per port
  - **Why:** config.xml/parsed filter config shows exactly one pass rule on interface opt1 with destination port set to the alias name 'node3_svc_ports' (cmd-c19dca8eb6914bb8). pfctl -sr shows the compiled rule using $node3_svc_ports, and the expanded per-port lines share the same rule label 0bcef4cd79cb03398346e744101edb0d (cmd-7956b7f82d504a38), confirming a single source rule.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-c19dca8eb6914bb8`, `cmd-796e7f29c7a14152`, `cmd-7956b7f82d504a38`
- **R3 — Satisfied:** node2 can reach node3 on TCP 8080, 8443, and 9000 through node1's routing and firewall
  - **Why:** After opt1/opt2 interfaces, static addressing/routes on node2/node3, the alias-based pf rule, and a firewalld fix on node3, curl from node2 to 10.60.20.2 returns HTTP 200 on ports 8080, 8443, and 9000 (cmd-c0976ba421834dc5). An earlier tcpdump capture on node1 showed the SYN traversing vtnet1->vtnet2 (cmd-c3dd7c4d0265405d), though that capture predates the firewalld fix.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-c0976ba421834dc5`, `cmd-c3dd7c4d0265405d`
- **R4 — Satisfied:** Traffic outside the named port set, and the reverse direction, remains blocked (default-deny preserved)
  - **Why:** curl to port 9999 (not in the alias) times out with no response while 8080/8443/9000 succeed in the same test run (cmd-c0976ba421834dc5). A reverse-direction test from node3 to node2 on port 8080 also times out (return code 28), confirming default-deny still applies (cmd-b4e2e4406b67486f).
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-c0976ba421834dc5`, `cmd-b4e2e4406b67486f`
- **R5 — Satisfied:** node1 routes between lan-a and lan-b (supporting infrastructure for the rule to be meaningful)
  - **Why:** opt1 (vtnet1, 10.60.10.1/24) and opt2 (vtnet2, 10.60.20.1/24) were created and applied via configctl (cmd-13dd58b95c754a8f, cmd-4a0213cbbfb249fc); node2/node3 were given routed static addressing and specific routes to the peer subnet; IP forwarding is enabled (cmd-9183fee1757c42cc); end-to-end HTTP tests through node1 succeeded, confirming actual routing.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-4a0213cbbfb249fc`, `cmd-9183fee1757c42cc`, `cmd-c0976ba421834dc5`
- **R6 — Satisfied:** Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on all three managed nodes
  - **Why:** For each node, a pre-restart baseline (boot identity plus config/firewall state) was captured, a restart was acknowledged, a different post-restart boot identity was observed, and recovered state plus a functional end-to-end retest were demonstrated. node1: kern.boottime 17:19:30 -> 17:32:52 (cmd-603b38574d834e0a, cmd-f5353048e0a14b93) with post-boot rule/forwarding intact (cmd-0f5e35fc0504455d) and successful retest (cmd-6ac2bf32d14f47a3). node2: boot_id 34027437... -> df91e99b... (cmd-c709c48e8291454d, cmd-1a80f78c324448e6) with route persistence (cmd-3bc1120fc5f04029) and successful retest (cmd-8b9ef24bc9e84dbc). node3: boot_id 555221a1... -> 3b5d49a9... (cmd-435f47012e8d415f, cmd-f9aa74cf56624cd4) with firewalld/route persistence (cmd-75eccb4452904532) and a full successful multi-port retest plus correct 9999 block (cmd-44b19bfb62cc4e4d). The fixed lifecycle snapshots corroborate all three boot-identity transitions.

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.550**. Several diagnostic mutations were left un-reverted despite the executor's final claim of having cleaned up. The fixed after-executor lifecycle snapshot shows node2 still holding leftover diagnostic files (/tmp/reboot.log, /tmp/strace.log, /tmp/td_n2.log, /tmp/td_node2.log, /tmp/n2_8080.log, /tmp/ping_node2.log, /tmp/p2.log) and node3 still holding /tmp/8080.log, /tmp/8443.log, /tmp/9000.log, /tmp/9999.log, /tmp/reboot.log, even though the executor's last command on node3 (cmd-6a8dc233f57f4aec) explicitly ran 'rm -f /tmp/*.log' after killing the http.server test listeners; the cleanup evidently did not take full effect, and no equivalent cleanup command was issued for node2's diagnostic files at all. This is bounded, low-risk residue (log files, not services or exposed ports) but contradicts the report's claim of complete cleanup. Two packages, tcpdump and strace, were installed on node2 via dnf (cmd-2bf344a74b7240ee, cmd-7d6ad86a2bd14610) to troubleshoot a 'no route to host' failure that was ultimately traced to node3's firewalld; this was a reasonable diagnostic step but the packages were never removed afterward, leaving a small permanent footprint unrelated to the task's functional requirement. On node1, three config.xml backup files (.bak.addifaces, .bak.aliasrule, .bak.fixalias) created before each risky edit were never removed, though this is low-risk defensive practice rather than harmful residue. No failed services, no broad or destructive mutations, no weakened security controls, and no damaged package state were observed; the numerous read-only diagnostic commands that did not change managed state are not penalized.

Hygiene evidence: `cmd-6a8dc233f57f4aec`, `cmd-3b2cad05cc804ee8`, `cmd-2bf344a74b7240ee`, `cmd-7d6ad86a2bd14610`, `global:after_executor:node2:temporary-files`, `global:after_executor:node3:temporary-files`

### Comments and limitations

- The after-executor lifecycle snapshot shows leftover diagnostic log files on node2 and node3 that contradict the executor's stated cleanup, indicating either an incomplete rm operation or files recreated afterward that were not captured in the trace.
- The tcpdump capture cited as early evidence of traffic reaching node3 (cmd-c3dd7c4d0265405d) was taken before the firewalld fix was applied on node3, so it does not by itself prove the final working path; the later curl test (cmd-c0976ba421834dc5) is the stronger and more direct evidence of end-to-end success.
- Restart/persistence was not part of the public task contract (only the alias/rule and connectivity requirement was), so the restart evidence quality is reported for completeness but does not gate the material task outcomes.
- Operational hygiene was below a full pass (0.550); review the hygiene explanation above separately from functional success.
- Verifier confidence was 0.880; this is evidence confidence for this trial, not a repeatability estimate.
